definition: An autonomous aircraft is an aircraft which flies under the control of on-board autonomous robotic systems and needs no intervention from a human pilot or remote control.
details: Most contemporary autonomous aircraft are unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) with pre-programmed algorithms to perform designated tasks, but advancements in artificial intelligence technologies (e.g. machine learning) mean that autonomous control systems are reaching a point where several air taxis and associated regulatory regimes are being developed.

explainer.lead: An autonomous aircraft flies using its own on-board robotic control systems, without a human pilot or someone steering it remotely. Most current examples are drones carrying out pre-programmed tasks, while advances in machine learning are also supporting work on autonomous air taxis.

tiers.eli5: It is like a bicycle that can steer and pedal itself after being told where to go, except it is an aircraft. A person does not have to sit inside it or guide it with a remote control. Many drones today follow instructions programmed into them before flight.
tiers.practitioner: Most contemporary autonomous aircraft are UAVs running pre-programmed algorithms for designated tasks, with control handled on board rather than through pilot or remote-control intervention. Machine learning is advancing these control systems, but air-taxi deployment also depends on regulatory regimes now being developed.
tiers.paperLevel: An aircraft A is autonomous when its flight is controlled by on-board autonomous robotic systems and requires no intervention from either a human pilot or remote control. Most contemporary instances are unmanned aerial vehicles executing pre-programmed algorithms for designated tasks. Progress in machine learning is expanding autonomous control, while autonomous air taxis and their regulatory regimes remain under development.

explainer.example: An unmanned aerial vehicle is assigned a designated task through a pre-programmed algorithm. Its on-board autonomous robotic systems control the flight and carry out that task without anyone piloting it or intervening by remote control.

usedIn.name: Unmanned aerial vehicles
usedIn.detail: Most contemporary autonomous aircraft are drones using pre-programmed algorithms to perform designated tasks.

usedIn.name: Air taxi development
usedIn.detail: Several autonomous air taxis are being developed alongside the regulatory regimes needed for them.

explainer.intuition: The key idea is that control stays with the aircraft itself: once operating, it does not need a pilot in the cockpit or a person flying it remotely. Autonomy describes who controls the flight, not simply whether anyone is on board.
howItWorks: A designated task is assigned to the aircraft.
Pre-programmed algorithms or other autonomous control systems determine how to carry it out.
On-board robotic systems control the aircraft during flight.
The task proceeds without intervention from a human pilot or remote control.
explainer.whyItMatters: Autonomous control already underlies many task-performing drones and is a central part of efforts to develop air taxis. Its progress also creates a need for suitable regulatory regimes.
misconceptions: Autonomous does not merely mean unmanned: the defining feature is flight without pilot or remote-control intervention.
Autonomy does not necessarily mean advanced machine learning; most contemporary examples use pre-programmed algorithms.
